# Cross-language crypto interop fixture

`crypto_interop.json` is **generated by the TypeScript control plane itself**,
not hand-computed from the algorithm description. It is produced by running the
compiled `CryptoService`
(`apps/control-api/dist/common/crypto.service.js` — the same file NestJS loads
at runtime) and capturing the envelopes it emits.

Regenerate after any change to `apps/control-api/src/common/crypto.service.ts`:

```sh
cd apps/control-api && pnpm build      # refresh dist/
node services/data-plane/internal/worker/testdata/generate_crypto_fixture.js \
  > services/data-plane/internal/worker/testdata/crypto_interop.json
```

`crypto_interop_test.go` decrypts every vector with the Go implementation and
asserts the plaintext, so a divergence in the envelope format, the base64url
alphabet, the AES-GCM parameters or — the likely one — the additional
authenticated data fails the Go test suite rather than every webhook signature
in production.

The keys in the fixture are literal ASCII strings (`0123456789abcdef…`) chosen
so they are obviously test material. They are not, and must never be, a real
`ENCRYPTION_KEY`.
